0.0.n: This borrowed word refers to animation, especially Japanese animation in English usage.

0.1.n: Adds anime to other things the speaker likes.

0.2.n: Expresses a strong liking; the person who feels this is left unstated.

0.3.n: The linking form of だ connects 大好き to the next statement.

1.0.n: Placed before 好き to show the highest degree of liking.

1.1.n: Together with 一番, it describes the work the speaker likes best.

1.2.n: Connects 好き to the noun 作品 so it can describe that noun.

1.3.n: Refers to a creative work, here an anime series.

1.4.n: Marks the speaker’s favorite work as the topic.

1.5.n: Part of the title 進撃の巨人, officially called Attack on Titan in English.

1.6.n: Links 進撃 to 巨人 within the title; English reverses their order in a literal rendering.

1.7.n: Means a giant and forms part of the anime title 進撃の巨人.

1.8.n: Politely ends the statement identifying the speaker’s favorite work.

2.0.n: Directly addresses the listener; Japanese often omits this when the listener is clear.

2.1.n: Here の marks あなた as the person who likes the anime, rather than simply showing ownership.

2.2.n: Describes the listener’s preference; unlike line 1, no word explicitly says most.

2.3.n: Connects 好き to アニメ, making it anime that the listener likes.

2.4.n: Names the category of entertainment the speaker is asking about.

2.5.n: Marks anime the listener likes as the topic of the question.

2.6.n: Read as なん before です, it asks the listener to identify an anime.

2.7.n: Makes the question polite when followed by か.

2.8.n: Placed at the end to turn the sentence into a question.

3.0.n: Adds warmth and eagerness to the request rather than making it a command.

3.1.n: The て-form of 教える plus ください makes a polite request; here 教える means tell rather than teach.

0.lit: Anime too, I am very fond of, and…
0.tip: で links the description 大好き to the next sentence rather than ending the thought.

1.lit: As for the work I like most, it is Titan of the Advance.
1.tip: 一番好きな作品 means the work I like best; 進撃の巨人 is the title Attack on Titan.

2.lit: As for anime that you like, what is it?
2.tip: あなたの好きなアニメ means anime you like; の marks who likes it inside this phrase.

3.lit: By all means, please tell me.
3.tip: A verb’s て-form followed by ください is a standard way to make a polite request.
